strap: A daily dispatch from the world you are entering

lead.title: Discretion appears in 61.3 per cent of American household briefs, three times more often than any qualification
lead.standfirst: A new study of 465 United States staffing briefs finds that families write down trust and private household experience far more often than a certificate, and that the roles carrying the widest remit ask for the longest record.
lead.body:
Morgan & Mallet published on 18 August the fullest picture yet of what American families actually write down when they ask an agency to find someone. The firm analysed 465 United States job briefs recorded between May 2022 and June 2026, each one a client's request to recruit for a single role. The single most frequent requirement was not a skill at all. Discretion or confidentiality appeared in 61.3 per cent of briefs. Previous private household experience followed at 58.5 per cent. A formal qualification or certification appeared in 20.4 per cent, roughly a third as often as discretion.

The practical skills sit underneath that. Laundry and ironing appeared in 43.2 per cent of briefs, cooking in 41.3 per cent, events and entertaining in 31.6 per cent. The ordering matters more than the individual figures. A family can teach a house its own way of pressing a shirt. It cannot teach judgment, and it cannot un-hear a conversation that left the property. The report's authors put it plainly: skills help someone carry out the role, while trust and an understanding of family life let them complete the work without adding to the family's mental load.

Experience requirements climb with responsibility rather than with prestige. Across the roles measured, families asked for a minimum of four years. Butler and formal service briefs carried the highest average minimum at 6.7 years, followed by household and estate management at 6.3 years, then nanny and childcare at 4.7 years, transport at 4.6 years and housekeeping at 4.5 years. These are the positions where someone welcomes guests, leads a team, coordinates contractors and keeps the house running while the principals are elsewhere, and the length of record families ask for reflects exactly that.

A smaller set of briefs asks for something narrower still. Fine dining or Michelin kitchen experience appeared in 7.5 per cent, yacht experience in 5.2 per cent, formal or silver service in 3.7 per cent, Montessori training in 2.2 per cent and smart home systems in 1.3 per cent. These requirements are rare across the whole sample but decisive for the household that writes them, because they define the entire search. A candidate who holds one of them holds a key to a very small door.

The methodology is worth stating, since the numbers will be quoted loosely elsewhere. The data covers one agency's American assignments, and a brief records a client's request rather than a confirmed placement. It is not a census of every private household in the United States. It is, however, an unusually direct record of what families say they want before anyone has been interviewed.
lead.why: The list of requirements is effectively the order in which a candidate should build a career: discretion and private household experience first, technical skills second, certificates third. A qualification opens a conversation. A record of confidentiality is what keeps the post.
lead.src: Morgan & Mallet, Inside the Modern Private Household, US Household Staffing Report 2026

articles.title: The Hamptons sells 378 houses in a quarter, 21 per cent fewer than last year, and the median price still rises by almost a third
articles.body:
The second quarter figures for the East End describe a market that is contracting in volume and expanding in price at the same time. A total of 378 properties changed hands between April and June, a fall of 21.1 per cent on the same period in 2025. Total dollar volume came in at approximately USD 1.45 billion, down 11.9 per cent. On those two numbers alone the season looks weak.

The price data says the opposite. The average sale price rose 11.7 per cent year on year to USD 3.84 million. The median rose far harder, up 31.9 per cent to USD 2.5 million. When the median climbs three times faster than the average, the explanation is usually compositional rather than inflationary: the cheaper transactions have stopped happening, so the middle of the market has moved up the ladder rather than the ladder itself moving.

That is precisely what the report describes. The shortage is concentrated below USD 3 million, where there is very little to buy, while activity above USD 3 million has held up and carried the quarter. Fewer closings, not falling values. The East End has also been changing character for some years, as New York families who once treated a Hamptons house as a summer address now keep it as a primary or year-round residence.

For anyone who runs a house out there, the second point is the operational one. A seasonal property is opened in May and closed in October, and its staffing follows that rhythm. A year-round property needs heating plant that works in February, a contractor list that answers in the off season, a security arrangement for an empty house in midwinter and a household team that is not hired on a summer contract. The transition from one model to the other is rarely announced. It is discovered by whoever is holding the keys in January.
articles.why: A market where houses are held longer and used year round changes the shape of the job attached to them, from a seasonal opening and closing to a permanent operation with winter maintenance, off-season contractors and a team that does not disperse in September.
articles.src: Hamptons Prive, on the Brown Harris Stevens Hamptons second quarter 2026 market report

articles.title: The family office moves towards lean structures and direct ownership, and the house is expected to feel as frictionless as the portfolio
articles.body:
Knight Frank's 2026 Family Office Survey, published in April as part of the twentieth edition of The Wealth Report, draws on interviews with more than 40 family offices in London, New York, Dubai, Singapore, Hong Kong and beyond. The sector it describes is growing quickly and remains remarkably varied in how it operates, but the direction of travel is towards structure: explicit targets, formal processes and decisions taken on analysis rather than instinct.

Three changes sit underneath that. Co-investment is spreading, letting offices share risk and reach larger opportunities than they could alone. Professionalisation is advancing, with many offices now employing internal specialists in private equity, venture capital and real estate rather than outsourcing the judgment. And portfolios keep widening, combining liquid assets with private equity, venture capital, infrastructure and direct property. Direct ownership of real estate remains attractive precisely because it lets a family shape a development strategy and keep the whole of the upside instead of sharing it through a fund.

The survey also records a preference the household will feel directly. Knight Frank calls it frictionless wealth: a move towards lighter, more flexible structures, mirroring a broader shift in ultra-wealthy life towards convenience and immediacy. Several offices are applying the same principle internally, keeping the permanent team small and buying in outside expertise when an opportunity appears. A rising generation wants to see its positions live, daily, with currency overlay, rather than in a quarterly pack.

London appears in the survey as a city under pressure rather than a city in decline. Sentiment is more cautious than it was a decade ago, yet almost nobody interviewed expects the city's importance to disappear, and its financial depth, connectivity and time zone remain powerful anchors in an era when families keep several bases at once. Dubai, Hong Kong and Singapore are gaining ground alongside New York, not instead of London.

A lean office has a consequence that rarely appears in the research. When the permanent headcount is deliberately small, the work does not vanish. It settles on whoever is closest to the principal and already trusted, which in practice means the house manager, the estate manager or the senior assistant. The frictionless family is frictionless because someone absorbs the friction.
articles.why: Smaller, flatter family offices push more coordination onto the household team. The person running the house increasingly holds tasks that a larger office would have kept in-house, which raises both the standard expected and the value of the post.
articles.src: Knight Frank, Family Office Survey 2026, The Wealth Report

articles.title: Cannes opens the autumn season on 8 September with around 700 boats and 150 world premieres
articles.body:
The Cannes Yachting Festival returns for its 49th edition from 8 to 13 September, opening the international boating season two weeks before Monaco. More than 680 exhibitors are expected, with a fleet of roughly 700 boats from 5 to 50 metres, and around 150 world premieres. It remains Europe's leading in-water show and the principal fixture for vessels of 500 gross tonnes and below.

The layout is unchanged in principle and matters for anyone arranging a client's visit. The Vieux Port takes the motor segment, from 12 to 50 metres, together with superyachts, rigid inflatables and catamarans, with large yachts on the Quai Max Laubeuf and the redesigned Jetee holding in-water yachts and engine manufacturers. Port Canto takes sail above 10 metres, the brokerage fleet, smaller motorboats and the water toys area. A regular maritime shuttle runs between the two, which is the detail that decides whether an afternoon of appointments is feasible or not.

The 2026 edition is the first under Constance Brement, a new director drawn from the nautical and luxury sectors, whose stated aim is to widen the show's international reach and improve the visitor experience. The programme leans hard on the energy transition. The Innovation Route runs a dedicated trail through efficiency, sustainability and propulsion, judged by an international panel of professionals and journalists, with awards for navigation equipment, sustainable products, innovative boats and corporate responsibility. The finalists of the Best of Boat Awards are announced on 9 September at six in the evening.

Cannes is the show where a family that charters decides what it wants to charter next, and where a first boat is often bought. For the household side, September in the Riviera means diaries that fill in fifteen minute blocks, tender movements between two ports, and a week in which the principal's schedule is set by a shuttle timetable rather than by the house.
articles.why: Boat show weeks are among the densest logistical periods in the private calendar. Knowing which port holds which segment, and that a shuttle links them, is the difference between a schedule that works and one that collapses by mid-morning.

articles.title: Frieze Seoul opens its fifth edition on 2 September with more than 125 galleries, and Asia keeps the first week of the art year
articles.body:
Frieze Seoul returns to COEX in Gangnam from 2 to 5 September, in partnership with Kiaf SEOUL. The fifth edition brings together more than 125 galleries from 30 countries, with over 70 per cent of participants based across the Asia-Pacific region and more than 50 exhibitors holding permanent spaces in Seoul itself. The Galleries section alone gathers over 85 international houses, among them Hauser & Wirth, Pace, White Cube, David Zwirner, Lisson, Thaddaeus Ropac, Gladstone, Lehmann Maupin and Sprueth Magers, alongside the leading Korean names including Kukje, Gallery Hyundai, PKM, Arario and Hakgojae.

Two curated sections are new this year. Material Practice, curated by Hyeyoung Cho, sits at the intersection of contemporary art and design and draws on Seoul's traditions of craft and material innovation. Spotlight, curated by Wonseok Koh, arrives at Frieze Seoul for the first time and is devoted to solo presentations of twentieth century artists, foregrounding overlooked figures and art-historical narratives outside the dominant Western canon. Focus, now in its fourth year and advised by Seolhui Lee, presents 16 galleries founded in or after 2014, and expands beyond Asia for the first time.

The fair is only part of the week. Neighborhood Nights run from 31 August to 3 September, moving each evening through a different district: Euljiro on the Monday, Hannam on the Tuesday, Cheongdam on the Wednesday and Samcheong on the Thursday, with late openings, performances and events. Museum programming across the city includes Koo Jeong A at the Leeum Museum of Art, Do Ho Suh at MMCA Seoul, Sol LeWitt at the Amorepacific Museum of Art and Es Devlin at FUTURA Seoul. Deutsche Bank continues as global lead partner, in the 23rd year of that arrangement.

The practical shape of the week is the point. A principal who attends is not attending a fair, but a five day itinerary spread across four districts, with invitation-only hours on the Wednesday, preview access on the Thursday morning and public opening only from three in the afternoon on that day. Anyone building the diary needs to know which door opens at which hour, because at Frieze the difference between the preview and the public opening is the difference between seeing a work and reading about it.
articles.why: Cultural fluency is not knowing that a fair exists but knowing how its week is structured. Preview tiers, neighbourhood evenings and museum openings are the raw material of a well-built diary for a collecting family.

articles.title: Three states hold almost two thirds of American household briefs, and the Florida hiring season starts this month
articles.body:
The same Morgan & Mallet analysis maps where the American work actually sits, and the concentration is severe. California accounted for 24.1 per cent of United States briefs, Florida for 23.0 per cent and New York for 16.1 per cent, with a clear drop to Texas and Georgia behind them. Yet New York City, Miami and Los Angeles together made up only 33.8 per cent of briefs. Two thirds of the searches happen somewhere other than the three obvious cities.

The list of top locations makes the point. Braselton in Georgia came fourth, ahead of San Francisco, and recorded the largest increase in share of any city in 2025, rising 8.0 percentage points against the 2023 to 2024 period. Belle Vernon in Pennsylvania, Palm Beach, Tampa, Greenwich and Washington DC completed the top ten. Within the leading states the settings vary enormously, from Malibu and Atherton to Jupiter Island, East Hampton and Old Westbury. Household staffing follows the properties a family uses, not the cities a map would suggest.

The working arrangements are less uniform than the trade assumes. Of briefs that specified an employment basis, 95.2 per cent were full time, and where permanence was stated, 93.3 per cent sought a permanent hire. Living arrangements split three ways: 39.6 per cent live-in, 32.5 per cent live-out and 28.0 per cent open to either. In New York in particular, families increasingly prefer live-out staff, because apartment space is scarce and a local who already knows the city is more useful than one who needs housing.

Season matters more than most candidates realise. Florida's hiring runs opposite to the north east, because the snowbird households arriving from Massachusetts, New York, Connecticut and Canada need to be staffed by October. The recruitment high season there therefore begins in August and September, which is to say now. Staff rotate between properties and follow the principals, so a candidate willing to move with a household has a market that reopens twice a year rather than once.

Two structural facts sit behind all of it. Estate managers account for roughly one in ten American requests and remain among the hardest posts to fill, in part because the estate manager usually goes on to build the rest of the team. And average tenure in private service has fallen from around 20 years to nearer three, which means the candidate who can show five years or more with one family now stands out rather than blends in.
articles.why: Knowing the geography and the calendar of demand is a hiring advantage in itself. A candidate who understands that Florida staffs up in late summer, and that half the work sits outside the famous cities, can time an approach rather than wait for one.
articles.src: Morgan & Mallet, US Household Staffing Report 2026 and 2026 US salary guidance

briefs.b: Global Jet Capital's second quarter market brief puts business jet availability at 6.6 per cent of the fleet, down from 6.7 per cent in the first quarter and well below the historical average of roughly 10 per cent. Listings rose 3.3 per cent year on year, but the growth came from older aircraft while supply of jets aged 12 years and under tightened further. Departures rose 3.4 per cent across the first half, led by fractional operators.
briefs.src: GlobalAir, on Global Jet Capital data, 19 August 2026

briefs.b: Frieze confirmed this month that Frieze Seoul will move from COEX to the Dongdaemun Design Plaza from 2027. The 2026 edition is therefore the last at the Gangnam venue that has hosted the fair since it launched. Anyone planning a family's art calendar beyond this year should note the change of district.

Where an American brief specified a language, English appeared in 75.8 per cent of them. French followed at 26.8 per cent and Spanish at 25.5 per cent, with Italian at 7.2 per cent. Families often ask for more than one, so the figures overlap, and a second language remains one of the cheapest differentiators a candidate can hold.
briefs.src: Morgan & Mallet, US Household Staffing Report 2026

briefs.b: Butler and formal service briefs carried the highest average minimum experience requirement of any role measured, at 6.7 years, ahead of household and estate management at 6.3 years. Nanny and childcare briefs asked for 4.7 years, transport 4.6 and housekeeping 4.5. Across all roles the floor sat at about four years.
briefs.src: Morgan & Mallet, US Household Staffing Report 2026
